question: Can the actual neutral opposite-circulation belt share native canonical rim dynamics with the original branch?
source_operation: Per-face branch conjugation of the selected intrinsic mode, in unchanged real triangle plane axes; source nonzero selected numerators determine the coordinatewise complex-linear unit-phase candidate D_j=z'_j/z_j.
carriers: Two pointed 36-complex-dimensional numerator carriers with metric diag(1/d), the same labelled native geometry and C3; a retained 16-complex-dimensional record bank with its original Gram metric. No physical time or continuum completion is asserted.
bold_conjecture: A single metric-preserving branch adapter transports native L/G/N, seam mismatch energies, addressed rim pulses and the occupied canonical closure. Test the unchanged phase-character law separately rather than assume it transports.
rivals: Partial conjugation is necessary and destroys one common symplectic form.

Every L/G/N coefficient, every one of 21 independently rebuilt seam projectors, and all 18 frame-addressed canonical projectors must intertwine exactly.

Rebuild native phase defects using the original real geometry cycle and independently supplied face signs; compare both fixed omega and signed omega, not a Hamiltonian defined merely by conjugating the old answer.

hostiles: Identity adapter must fail on changed L/N.
